verdict.detail: Correction to this morning's briefing, on Georg's prompt. Four of the eleven did not start the most recent matchday, not the three I reported, and I had the two matchdays the wrong way round. The action does not change — hold the Pinckert offer, sell nothing before it resolves, because all capacity is committed and the eleven-player floor blocks every sale. But the reason to hold is now stronger, not weaker: the fallback if the funding leg slips tonight turns out to be close to free rather than costly.

sell.reason: Still one sale, still conditional, still the same man: the injured midfielder, and only once the purchase has landed, because his market value is literally what pays for it. The tempting reaction to the new findings is to swap the funding sale to the demoted forward instead, since the two are priced within a couple of hundred thousand of each other. That would be wrong. Selling the forward keeps an injured player with no return date in the fielded eleven; selling the midfielder keeps a fit player who is at least getting minutes. Keep the fit one. The old shape comparison had these two paths within three points of each other and treated the choice as near-indifferent; the selection evidence breaks the tie decisively. Nothing else can be sold at eleven players. Once the squad reaches twelve or more the order is: the defender with no starts all season first, then the benched defender — whose price is still rising, so the market has not marked the benching in yet, which is exactly when to sell rather than after it does — then the demoted forward.
